scope: Proposition 6.1 (End approximation) of the manuscript “The Penrose inequality for maximal asymptotically hyperbolic initial data” (preprints/The-Penrose-inequality-for-maximal-asymptotically-hyperbolic-initial-data-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 641d4aa3892adbca), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under (6.1), there are smooth metrics gj on the same exterior such that Rgj > −6, Hgj (S) ≤ 0, gj → g locally in C2, and (1 − ϵj)g ≤ gj ≤ (1 + ϵj)g, ϵj ↓ 0, p0(gj) −→ p0(g). (6.3) Each gj has the required weighted scalar integrability and finite mass fluxes. Outside a compact set, depending on j, it is of the form gj = ϕ4 j b, ϕj = 1 + αj(ω)r−3 + O(r−3−ξ ), (6.4) where ξ > 0 can be fixed and the remainder has the same decay after any fixed finite number of angular and radial-logarithmic derivatives. In particular Amin(S; gj) → Amin(S; g).
